desc:
CRM sales automation workflows handle the small repeat jobs your team does every day. Ecom Swift LLC builds and tests automations in your CRM that create tasks, update fields, notify owners and queue messages for approval.

## What are CRM sales automations?

CRM sales automations are rules that say "when this happens, do that" inside your CRM. A deal moves to a new stage and a task appears. A lead stays quiet and the owner gets nudged. A deal is won and the fields, checklists and handover steps update by themselves.

They do not replace salespeople. They take over the routine work around the conversation, so people can spend their attention on the conversation itself.

## Where busywork hides in a sales team

Look at a normal week and you will find the same actions repeated: setting a follow-up date, copying a deal value into another field, telling a colleague that a customer signed, creating a delivery checklist. Each takes a minute. Added together they take hours, and they get skipped whenever someone is busy.

When steps are skipped, the CRM drifts away from reality. A won deal without a handover leaves the delivery team guessing. A stage change without a task leaves a lead without a next step. Automation makes the boring parts happen every time.

## How automation improves speed and consistency

The main benefit is reliability. A rule does not forget on a Friday afternoon or when it is on holiday. Every deal in a stage gets the same treatment, which makes your process real instead of aspirational.

It also creates time. Less data entry means salespeople contact more people and write better messages. Managers gain cleaner records without chasing updates. And because workflows run on conditions, they can differ by deal value or lead source, so a large opportunity gets more attention than a small one.

## What a well-built automation set includes

- Task creation when a deal enters a stage, with an owner and due date.
- Notifications to the deal owner or a manager on important events.
- Conditions based on deal value, source, region or product.
- Automatic field updates, such as a stage date or a status flag.
- Reminders when a lead has had no activity for a set period.
- A won deal handover checklist for the team that delivers the work.
- A welcome message queued for approval, never sent without a person checking it.
- Error alerts to one named admin if a workflow fails.
- A one line description for every workflow, so nobody wonders what it does.

## How we build and test them

We start by listing the tasks your team repeats, then rank them by how often they occur and how much time they waste. The best candidates are frequent, rule based and low risk. We write each one in plain words first, such as "when a deal reaches Proposal sent, create a task for the owner due in three days", and you confirm the wording.

Then we build the workflow in your CRM and test it on sample records. We move deals through every path, including the ones that should not trigger anything, because a rule that fires when it should not is worse than none. The Basic package covers a small set of simple automations. Standard adds more workflows with conditions and field updates. Premium adds an approval step before any customer message, a handover checklist and error alerts, along with a short period of fixes.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the jobs that happen daily.
- Keep a person in the loop before any message reaches a customer.
- Give each workflow a clear name and a one line description.
- Test with sample records before the real ones.
- Review the workflows when your process changes.

**Avoid:**
- Automating a process that nobody has agreed on.
- Building long chains where one change breaks six steps.
- Sending automatic emails to customers without a review.
- Stacking several rules that trigger on the same event.
- Leaving workflows running that nobody remembers creating.

## Who this service is for

It suits a team of two to twenty people that already uses a CRM but still does most admin by hand. It suits a manager who wants every deal to follow the same handover steps. It also suits an owner who is tired of correcting the same field mistakes every week.

## What we need from you

Give us a list of the repeat tasks that annoy your team, and describe what should happen in each case. We need access to your CRM as an admin or similar user, plus a note of any other apps you want connected, since the available connections depend on your plan. We never ask for passwords. Tell us who should receive error alerts, and who approves any message that goes to a customer.
